How the overall wave propagates through the build:
• None: whole unit; order comes from fill only
• Planar: slice-by-slice like a scanner
• Spherical: grow or explode from center
• Cylindrical: outward from center, ignoring height
• Random: no clear flow; natural/noisy

Sequence start point:
• Min corner: from container origin (usually a corner)

• Bottom center: from ground up; good for trees/buildings

Fill path inside each slice:
• Linear scan: row by row like a printer
• Raster: rows then in-row; supports zigzag
• Radial: from slice center outward
• Spiral: circles around center
• Smooth noise: Perlin noise; natural chunks
• Flood: BFS from seed; fire/vine/growth feel

Which axis to scan within a row; the other axis is the row-advance direction.
E.g. in an XY layer, X scans rows along Y; Y scans rows along X.

Blocks per row advance.
1.0 = every block; 2.0 = every two blocks (coarser rows).
Row 1 left-to-right, row 2 right-to-left, like a printer carriage.

Flood spread start per layer:
• Layer center: from slice geometric center
• Layer min corner: from slice (minX,minY,minZ)
• Layer random: random block per layer
• Global random: one random point for whole container

Blend between Flow and Fill:
• 0%: fluid blend, soft layer transitions
• 100%: next layer starts only after current finishes

Tip:
0% = soft transition (like water)
100% = strict layers (must finish previous layer)
